newsitem.title: USA: Sonus says studies show EchoGen useful.
newsitem.headline: Sonus says studies show EchoGen useful.

text.p: Sonus Pharmaceuticals Inc said Thursday that clinical studies show EchoGen-enhanced ultrasound to be useful in distinguishing malignant from benign breast lesions.

In a separate release Thursday, Sonus also said it had filed a new drug application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for EchoGen (Perflenapent Emulsion), a fluorocarbon-based ultrasound contrast agent.
Licensed to Abbott Laboratories Inc, EchoGen was developed to enhance the clinical utility and cost-effectiveness of ultrasound procedures in radiology and cardiology, the company said.
Sonus added that the filing of the New Drug Application with the FDA "triggers $4,000,000 in milestone payments" from Abbott Labs under an agreement giving it rights to market EchoGen in the U.S.
The EchoGen-enhanced ultrasound "appears to be useful" in distinguishing lesions after suspicious lumps are discovered by mammography examination, Sonus said.
EchoGen has completed clinical testing in both cardiology and radiology applications, Sonus said, adding that the new application was for certain radiology and cardiology studies.
